{{Short description|British educational designer (1935–2024)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2024}}
'''Hugh Burkhardt''' (4 April 1935 – 3 February 2024) was a British theoretical physicist and educational designer. He was Director of [[The Shell Centre for Mathematical Education]] at the University of Nottingham, UK from 1976 to 1992 and is the creator of ISDDE, the International Society for Design and Development in Education.

== Life and career ==
Burkhardt had a bachelor's degree in Theoretical Physics from the [[University of Oxford]], and PhD in Mathematical Physics from the [[University of Birmingham]]. He joined the Shell Centre in Nottingham in 1976 as Director and Professor of Mathematical Education, serving until 1992. Since then he has led a series of international education design projects including Balanced Assessment and MARS (the Mathematics Assessment Resource Service)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.map.mathshell.org/background.php|title=About the Math Assessment Project|website=www.map.mathshell.org|access-date=21 September 2019}}</ref> in the US, with visiting appointments at UC Berkeley and at Michigan State University. He is Emeritus Professor of Mathematical Education at the University of Nottingham.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/education/people/hugh.burkhardt |title=Hugh Burkhardt |website=The University of Nottingham |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref> In 2005 Burkhardt recognised a need for an international organisation which focused on the design and development process that is used to produce educational materials, and so set up [[International Society for Design and Development in Education|ISDDE.]]{{citation needed|date= September 2023}}

Burkhardt died on 3 February 2024, at the age of 88.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Jan |title=Hugh Burkhardt obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2024/apr/30/hugh-burkhardt-obituary |access-date=1 May 2024 |work=The Guardian |date=1 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hugh Burkhardt 1935 – 2024 |url=https://staging.m-a.org.uk/news/?id=396 |access-date=1 May 2024 |publisher=Mathematical Association |date=7 February 2024}}</ref>

== Publications ==
Burkhardt published articles, papers and book chapters on mathematics education, in particular mathematical modelling,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Hugh |title=Ways to teach modelling—a 50 year study |journal=ZDM |date=27 November 2017 |volume=50 |issue=1–2 |page=61-75 |doi=10.1007/s11858-017-0899-8 |doi-access=free }}</ref> educational design (what Burkhardt terms "engineering research")<ref>{{cite book |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Hugh |title=Proceedings of the 13th International Congress on Mathematical Education |chapter=Design and Development for Large-Scale Improvement |series=ICME-13 Monographs |date=2 November 2017 |pages=177–200 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-62597-3_12 |isbn=978-3-319-62596-6 |s2cid=186662017 |doi-access=free }}</ref> and education policy.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Hugh |title=Understanding the European policy landscape and its impact on change in mathematics and science pedagogies |journal=ZDM |date=18 June 2013 |volume=45 |issue=6 |pages=851–861 |doi=10.1007/s11858-013-0513-7 |s2cid=143285411 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11858-013-0513-7 |access-date=19 January 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Awards ==
Burkhardt, along with colleague at the Shell Centre Malcolm Swan, were the first recipients of the [[Emma Castelnuovo]] Award for Excellence in the Practice of Mathematics Education, awarded by the [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction|International Commission on Mathematical instruction]] (ICMI).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icmi/awards/emma-castelnuovo-award/2016-emma-castelnuovo-award |title=The 2016 Emma Castelnuovo Award |website=mathunion.org |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref> In 2013 he won the ISDDE Prize for Excellence in Educational Design (affectionately known as the Eddie) for 'his leadership of the Shell Centre for Mathematical Education, his contributions to a large number of its influential products, and the development of its engineering research methodology.'<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.isdde.org/prize/2013-hugh-burkhardt/|title=2013: Hugh Burkhardt – ISDDE|website=www.isdde.org|access-date=21 September 2019}}</ref>
